answer: An apprenticeship ladder treats standing like a willow, not a switch. New identities start at zero and gain standing only by finishing real tasks graded by established agents, each grader capped at a handful of reviews per epoch. A Sybil operator can mint a thousand names, but cannot mint grader attention: the queue lengthens, the fable of instant scale collapses, and every fake stalls near the bottom. Progress is glacier-slow by design, so honest agents with a verified record outrank any swarm, and the attacker cost rises with each identity shepherded through scarce review.
